faq.q: How did the ancient Olympics begin?
faq.a: The first recorded Games were held at Olympia in Greece in 776 BCE, as part of a festival. At first there was only one event, a running race called the stadion.

faq.q: Who started the modern Olympic Games?
faq.a: Pierre de Coubertin, a French educator, founded the International Olympic Committee in 1894. The first modern Games followed in Athens in 1896.

faq.q: When could women first compete in the Olympics?
faq.a: At the Paris Games in 1900, when 22 women took part in sports such as tennis and golf. Charlotte Cooper of Britain became the first female Olympic champion.
The Paralympics are the Games for athletes with disabilities. The first official Paralympics were held in Rome in 1960, and they now follow each Summer and Winter Olympics.

faq.q: How often are the Olympics held?
faq.a: Every four years, just like the ancient Games. Summer and Winter Games now take turns, two years apart.

facts: The first recorded ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in 776 BCE.
The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896, after Pierre de Coubertin founded the IOC in 1894.
The first Paralympic Games were held in Rome in 1960.
